*Curriculum reference: NCDC Primary Seven Curriculum, Set One, English Topic 1 — School Holidays, 30 periods (pages 32–35). This app topic covers sub-topics 1A Holiday Plans and 1B Holiday Activities using the owner's question-and-answer notes.*

**Background:** During school holidays children meet different people whom they interact with at varying levels, and they carry out various activities. This topic equips learners with language skills and values to enable them to interact effectively with others.
**Main purpose of the topic:** It equips learners with language skills and values that help them interact effectively with others during holiday situations.
**By the end of this topic you should be able to:**

items: describe holiday plans and holiday activities using appropriate language
narrate, read and write texts, stories, poems and dialogues about holidays
use the near future (**am/is/are going to + verb**) correctly
use **question tags**, **reported speech**, **participles**, **adjectives**, the **active voice** and the **third conditional** correctly
spell holiday vocabulary correctly and present ideas logically
demonstrate responsibility, cooperation, sharing, care, respect and love

blocks.x: **1. What is a school holiday?**
A school holiday is a period when learners do not attend their normal school lessons.
**2. Why do schools have holidays?**
Schools have holidays to give learners and teachers time to rest and to take part in other useful activities.
**3. What can learners do during school holidays?**
Learners can:

items: visit relatives.
travel.
study.
attend remedial classes.
help with housework.
work on the family farm.
visit friends.
go on trips and tours.
attend camps.
take part in sports.
attend concerts and shows.
revise school work.
learn new skills.

blocks.x: **4. What is a holiday plan?**
A holiday plan is an arrangement of activities that a person intends to carry out during a holiday.
**5. Why should learners make holiday plans?**
Learners should make holiday plans so that they can use their holiday time properly and productively.
**6. What should a good holiday plan contain?**
A good holiday plan should contain:

items: activities to be done.
places to visit.
people to visit.

study or revision time.
household responsibilities.
recreation and rest.

blocks.x: **7. Why is planning important during a holiday?**
Planning helps a learner organise time, avoid wasting time and accomplish useful activities.
**8. What is a holiday activity?**
A holiday activity is something a person does during a school holiday.
**9. What is the difference between a holiday plan and a holiday activity?**
A holiday plan describes what someone intends to do, while a holiday activity is something actually done during the holiday.
**10. What is a holiday plan?**
A holiday plan is a list or arrangement of activities that a learner intends to carry out during the holiday.

blocks.x: **12. Why should holiday plans suit the family setting?**

**13. What is a programme?**
A programme is a planned list of activities and the times when they will take place.
**14. How can a programme help a learner during a holiday?**
It helps the learner organise activities and use time effectively.
**15. What is travel?**
Travel is the act of moving from one place to another.
**16. Why might learners travel during holidays?**
They may travel to:

items: visit relatives.
visit friends.
attend celebrations.
go on tours.
go to the countryside.
attend camps.

"Prepare for" means to get ready for something.

"Break off" means to stop or end something.

**22. What are remedial classes?**
Remedial classes are additional lessons intended to help learners improve areas in which they have difficulties.
**23. Why might a learner attend remedial classes during a holiday?**
A learner may attend remedial classes to improve performance in subjects or areas that need more practice.
**24. What does "end vacation" mean?**
It means to finish the holiday period and prepare to return to school.
**25. Who are relatives?**
Relatives are members of a person's family.
**26. Who are pen pals?**
Pen pals are people who regularly communicate with each other by writing letters or messages, often while living in different places.
**27. What does "up-country" mean?**
In the Ugandan context, "up-country" refers to places outside the main town or city where a person lives, especially other parts of the country.
**28. What is a town?**
A town is a built-up settlement that is larger than a village but generally smaller than a city.
**29. What does "urban" mean?**
Urban refers to areas associated with towns and cities.
**30. What does "rural" mean?**
Rural refers to areas in the countryside, usually away from large towns and cities.
**31. What is the difference between urban and rural areas?**
Urban areas are mainly towns and cities, while rural areas are mainly countryside areas and villages.
**32. What does "commence" mean?**
"Commence" means to begin or start.
**33. Make a sentence using "commence".**
The holiday programme will commence on Monday.
**34. What does "board" mean in travelling?**
To board means to get onto a bus, train, aeroplane, boat or other means of transport.
**35. Make a sentence using "board".**

**36. What is a birthday?**
A birthday is the day on which a person was born, celebrated each year.
**37. Why might a birthday appear in a holiday programme?**

**38. How can a learner talk about a future holiday plan?**
A learner can use the structure:
**am/is/are going to + verb**
**39. What does "going to" express in this topic?**
It is used to talk about a planned or intended future action.
**40. Give an example using "going to".**
I am going to visit my parents next holiday.
**41. Give another example.**
We are going to travel up-country during the holiday.
**42. Make a sentence using "is going to".**

**43. Make a sentence using "are going to".**
The children are going to visit their grandparents.
**44. Make a sentence using "am going to".**
I am going to revise Mathematics during the holiday.
**45. How do we form a negative sentence using "going to"?**
We use:
**am/is/are + not + going to + verb**
**46. Give an example.**
I am not going to travel this holiday.
**47. Give another example.**
They are not going to attend the concert.
**48. How do we ask a question using "going to"?**
We place the appropriate form of **be** before the subject.
**49. Give an example.**
Are you going to visit your relatives?
**50. Give another example.**
Is Mary going to attend the camp?
**51. What is a question tag?**
A question tag is a short question added to the end of a statement to confirm information or seek agreement.
**52. Give an example of a question tag about a holiday.**
You will go to the village next week, won't you?
**53. What is the question tag in "You will visit your aunt, won't you?"?**
The question tag is **"won't you?"**
**54. What is the main statement in "You will visit your aunt, won't you?"?**
The main statement is **"You will visit your aunt."**
**55. What is the general rule for question tags?**
A positive statement normally takes a negative question tag, while a negative statement normally takes a positive question tag.
**56. Give a positive statement with a negative tag.**
You are going to travel, aren't you?
**57. Give a negative statement with a positive tag.**
You aren't going to travel, are you?

**59. Add the correct question tag: Mary is going to Kampala, ______?**
isn't she?

won't they?

sections.title: E. Reported speech in holiday plans

blocks.x: **61. What is reported speech?**
Reported speech is used to tell someone what another person said without using the speaker's exact words.
**62. What is direct speech?**
Direct speech gives the exact words spoken by a person.
**63. Give an example of direct speech about a holiday.**
Peter said, "I am going to visit my uncle."
**64. Change into reported speech: Peter said, "I am going to visit my uncle."**
Peter said that he was going to visit his uncle.
**65. Why do we use reported speech?**
We use reported speech to tell another person what someone said.
**66. Change into reported speech: Mary said, "I am going to travel."**
Mary said that she was going to travel.
**67. Change into reported speech: John said, "I will visit my grandmother."**
John said that he would visit his grandmother.
**68. Change into direct speech: Sarah said that she was going to attend remedial classes.**
Sarah said, "I am going to attend remedial classes."
**69. What happens to pronouns when changing direct speech into reported speech?**
Pronouns may change according to who is reporting the speech.
**70. What happens to some verb tenses when direct speech is changed into reported speech?**
Some verb tenses normally change to agree with the reporting verb and the time of reporting.
**71. What is a participle?**
A participle is a form of a verb that can be used in verb phrases or as an adjective.
**72. What is the present participle?**
The present participle is usually formed by adding **-ing** to a verb.
**73. Give examples of present participles.**

items: travelling.
visiting.
studying.
preparing.
cooking.
playing.
revising.

blocks.x: **117. What is the third conditional?**
The third conditional is used to talk about an unreal or imagined situation in the past and its possible result.
**118. What is the basic structure of the third conditional?**
**If + past perfect tense, would have + past participle**
**119. Give the example used in the topic.**

**120. What does the sentence mean?**

**121. Give another example of the third conditional.**

**122. Give another example.**

**123. Complete: If I had gone to the farm, I ______ have helped my father.**

**124. Complete: If John had visited us, we would ______ welcomed him.**
have
**125. Complete: If she had revised, she ______ have passed the test.**
